diagnosis.claim_level: measured with the original text extracted from the repository, in scratch containers (read-only source mount, no cargo cache volume, no old snapshot mounted into the candidate target cache); limits below
diagnosis.method: env/pose-control.sh extracts the ORIGINAL functions by name from modules/maths/matrix.c and vector.c (get_identity_matrix3x3, normalise_any_3d_vector, get_3d_vector_cross_product, get_3d_transformation_matrix_from_face_normal_and_heading; sha256 in env/original_extract.sha256) into a surrogate (vec3d, matrix3x3, ASSERT empty) and drives them, and the production file's own statics (-DPRODUCTION_TEXT), with 2000 raw-word inputs built from integers and exact power-of-two scalings (identical on every target; verified), under round-toward-zero as the host's guard sets it, with the production flags (-std=gnu99 -fno-strict-aliasing -fwrapv -ftrivial-auto-var-init=zero, gcc-12 12.2.0, -O0/-O1/-O2). The Rust test transcription is not an input to this control.
findings: x64 (SSE, __FLT_EVAL_METHOD__ 0): original text and production text give the same 2000 results (the oracle: the Windows x64 original, per the project's declared rotor/numeric policy).

i686 x87 with production flags: original text at -O1 differs from the x64 words on 1990 of 2000 inputs and production text on 1999; the two differ from EACH OTHER on 1657: the i686 result of the same original expressions depends on the compilation context (static helpers inlined, variables kept in x87 registers) and is not one answer. O1 and O2 of the original text agree with each other; O0 and -fexcess-precision=standard agree with each other and with standard production text, yet still differ from x64 because x87 evaluates whole expressions extended.

i686 with SSE float math (-msse2 -mfpmath=sse, diagnostic only, not a production flag): original text and production text equal the x64 words on all 2000 at -O0/-O1/-O2: libm sin/cos and sqrt agree across the two targets, and the remaining difference is the evaluation model, not the libraries.
after the correction, the patched production text on x87 i686 at -O0, -O1, -O2 and -fexcess-precision=standard, and on x64, equals the x64 original words on all 2000 (the after_* rows).
diagnosis.classification: PRODUCTION defect on x87 targets (evaluation model); the Rust transcription in the test is NOT the defect: it is the x64 original's single-precision-per-operation evaluation and, built for i686 (SSE2), computes the same words as x64.
limits: The control evaluates ONE function family (the face-normal placement). The other corrected sites (sweep ends, boxes, speed test, magnitude) are covered by the differential test over 400 generated worlds, not by a separate original-text control.

No retail 32-bit MSVC/x87 behaviour is known or claimed: the original on historical 32-bit MSVC is not available here and 'unknown historical behaviour must remain unknown'. The oracle chosen is the Windows x64 original, the project's declared policy for the rotor kernel (ENV-HOST-ROTOR-CI-1) and the platform of the shipped module.
The scratch control is a surrogate compilation context, not the engine's code generation (compare the rotor control's stated limit).

The earlier scratch attempts are preserved in env/superseded: run1 failed to link (-lm before the source), run2 generated target-dependent inputs (float arithmetic in the driver), so its output was not comparable.
